- A line chart showing the number of defective products manufactured each day

You need to receive a notification when the daily percentage of defective products manufactured exceeds 3%.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: a subscription
an alert
a smart narrative visual

questions.question:
You have a Power BI semantic model named Model1 that uses Import storage mode.  
  
You need to decrease the size of Model1. The solution must **NOT** increase report query response times.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Remove unnecessary columns.
Unpivot unnecessary columns.
Rename unnecessary columns.
Change Model1 to DirectQuery storage mode.

questions.explanation:
Removing unnecessary columns reduces the amount of data stored in the Import semantic model while retaining Import mode’s in-memory query performance. Unpivoting may increase row count, renaming columns does not reduce stored data, and DirectQuery can add source-query latency.\
\
**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction) · [Semantic model modes in the Power BI service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-dataset-modes-understand)

You have a PBIX file that imports data from a Microsoft Excel data source located on a file share in a local network.  
  
You are informed that the Excel data source has been moved to a different location.  
  
You need to update the PBIX file so that it uses the new location.  
  
What are three ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From the Datasets settings of the Power BI service, configure the data source credentials.
From the Data source settings in Power BI Desktop, configure the file path.
From Current File in Power BI Desktop, configure the Data Load settings.
From Power Query Editor, use the formula bar to configure the file path for the applied step.
From Advanced Editor in Power Query Editor, configure the file path in the M code.

questions.explanation:
The Excel connector’s source location is part of the query’s source definition. Power BI Desktop can update that location through Data source settings, while Power Query can update the path in the Source applied step through the formula bar or directly in the query’s M code through Advanced Editor. Service credential settings control authentication, and Data Load settings control loading behavior rather than the file location.

**Learn more:** [Handling Data source path — Power Query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/handling-resource-path) · [Data sources in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/desktop-data-sources)

What should you create?

options.text: a one-to-many relationship from Date[date_id] to Sales[sales_date_id] and another one-to-many relationship from Date[date_id] to Weekly_Returns[week_id]
a one-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_date_id] to Date[date_id] and a one-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_ship_date_id] to Date[date_id]
an additional date table named ShipDate, a many-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_date_id] to Date[date_id], and a many-to-many relationship from Sales[sales_ship_date_id] to ShipDate[date_id]

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Power BI report with one page. That page includes two line charts and one bar chart.  
  
You need to ensure that users can perform the following actions for all three visuals:

Edit the interactions between the three visuals.
Enable personalization for the report.

questions.question:
You are reviewing a Power BI data model.  
  
You have a calculated table with the following definition:  
  
```DAX  
ProductList = INTERSECT ( ProductsGroupA, ProductsGroupB )  
```  
  
You need to determine the result of the DAX expression.  
  
Which rows are returned in `ProductList`?

options.text: all the rows in ProductsGroupB that have a matching row in ProductsGroupA
all the rows in both tables
all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have a matching row in ProductsGroupB
all the rows in ProductsGroupA that have no matching row in ProductsGroupB.

questions.explanation:
DAX `INTERSECT` returns the rows from the first table expression that are also present in the second table expression. Therefore, the returned rows originate from `ProductsGroupA` and must have a matching row in `ProductsGroupB`.\
\
**Learn more:** [INTERSECT function (DAX) — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/intersect-function-dax)

options.text: Merge Suppliers and LineItems.

questions.question:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a report that includes a bar chart and a column chart. The bar chart displays customer count by customer segment. The column chart displays sales by month.  
  
You need to ensure that, when a segment is selected in the bar chart, you can see which portion of the total monthly sales belongs to that customer segment.  
  
How should the visual interactions be configured on the column chart when the bar chart is selected?

options.text: highlight
filter
no impact

questions.explanation:
Cross-highlighting preserves each month’s total-sales column and emphasizes the portion associated with the selected customer segment. Cross-filtering would instead remove the nonselected segments, so the full monthly total would no longer be visible. Microsoft documents that cross-highlighting emphasizes related data without hiding the other data.

**Learn more:** [Create and use column charts in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualization-column-charts) · [Change how visuals interact in a Power BI report](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-reports-visual-interactions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Power BI report that uses row-level security (RLS).  
  
You need to delegate RLS membership maintenance to an Azure network security team. The solution must **NOT** give the Azure network security team the ability to manage reports, datasets, or dashboards.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Grant the Read and Build permissions for the Power BI datasets to the Azure network security team.
Configure custom instructions for the Request access feature that instructs users to contact the Azure network security team.
Instruct the Azure network security team to create security groups. Configure RLS to use the groups.
Add the Azure network security team as members of the RLS role.

questions.explanation:
Power BI RLS roles support Microsoft Entra security groups as role members. Assigning those groups to the RLS roles allows the Azure network security team to maintain group membership in Microsoft Entra ID, while Power BI content-management permissions remain unassigned. Microsoft guidance specifically recommends mapping security groups to semantic-model roles because group membership can be managed in Microsoft Entra ID and delegated to network administrators.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) guidance in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/rls-guidance) · [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Power BI report containing four pages.  
  
Each page includes a slicer for a field named **Country**.  
  
You need to ensure that when a user selects a country on page 1, that selection is retained on page 2 and page 3. The solution must ensure that page 4 is not affected by selections on the other pages.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Remove the Country slicer from page 1, page 2, and page 3. Add the Country field to the page-level filters.
Remove the Country slicer from page 1, page 2, and page 3. Add the Country field to the report-level filters.
Move the Country slicer from page 2 and page 3 to page 1.
Sync the Country slicer on page 1, page 2, and page 3.

questions.explanation:
Power BI Sync slicers can synchronize the Country slicers across selected report pages. Syncing only pages 1, 2, and 3 carries the user’s selection among those pages while excluding page 4 from the filter effect.

**Learn more:** [Slicers in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/visuals/power-bi-visualization-slicers)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Power BI model containing a table named Employee. The table includes the following data.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732319420-zhn7bfsg.png)  
  
Each employee has one manager, as indicated by the ParentEmployeeID column.  
  
All reporting paths lead to the CEO at the top of the organizational hierarchy.  
  
You need to create a calculated column that returns the number of levels from each employee to the CEO.  
  
Which DAX expression should you use?

options.text: PATHLENGTH(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]))
PATHITEM(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]),1,INTEGER)
PATHCONTAINS(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]),1)
PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID])

questions.explanation:
`PATH` returns the parent-child path for an employee, and `PATHLENGTH` returns the number of items in that path, including the employee. `PATHLENGTH(PATH(Employee[EmployeeID],Employee[ParentEmployeeID]))` therefore returns the employee's hierarchy level count to the CEO.

**Learn more:** [PATHLENGTH function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/pathlength-function-dax) · [PATH function (DAX)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/dax/path-function-dax)

One document library contains manufacturing reports stored as Microsoft Excel files. All of the manufacturing reports use the same data structure.  
  
You need to use Power BI Desktop to load only the manufacturing reports into a table for analysis.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Get data from a SharePoint folder and enter the site URL Select Transform, then filter by the folder path to the manufacturing reports library.

You create a Power BI report named RPT1 that includes sales data. The data has 10 million rows, and RPT1 contains 15 different visuals.  
  
Users report that RPT1 loads slowly.  
  
You need to investigate the cause of the issue.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Power Query Editor
Query Diagnostics
DAX query view
Performance analyzer

questions.explanation:
Performance Analyzer records the load time of every report visual and breaks it down into components such as DAX query execution, DirectQuery time, and visual rendering. It identifies the visuals or report operations responsible for slow loading.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Performance Analyzer to examine report performance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/performance-analyzer)

questions.question:
You create a Power BI report named RPT1 that includes sales data. The data has 10 million rows, and RPT1 contains 15 different visuals.  
  
Users report that RPT1 loads slowly.  
  
You need to investigate the cause of the issue.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DATEADD(Date[Date], -30, DAY))
CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DATESBETWEEN(Date[Date], Max('Date'[Date])-30, Max('Date'[Date])))
CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DATESMTD(Date[Date]))
CALCULATE(SUM(Sales[SalesAmount]), DISTINCTCOUNT(Date[Date]) = 31)

questions.explanation: DATESBETWEEN creates a continuous date range from 30 days before the maximum date through the maximum date, correctly calculating a rolling 31-day sum. DATEADD alone would incorrectly shift the filter context within the current selection rather than creating an inclusive date range.

questions.question:
You have a Power BI report that contains a visual displaying gross sales by date. Anomaly detection is enabled for the visual.  
  
No anomalies are being detected. You need to make anomaly detection more likely to identify anomalies in the report.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Increase the Expected range transparency setting.
Add a data field to the Legend field well.
Increase the Sensitivity setting.
Add a data field to the Secondary values field well.

questions.explanation:
A higher Sensitivity setting makes the anomaly-detection algorithm flag more deviations, including smaller departures from the expected range. Expected-range transparency only changes presentation, and adding fields to visual wells does not increase the detection algorithm’s sensitivity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use the Analytics pane in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-analytics-pane)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a Power BI sales report for your company’s NorthWest region sales territory. The data will be sourced from a view in a Microsoft SQL Server database. A sample of the data is shown in the following table:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730127565-ob46oice.png)  
  
The report will support the following analysis:  
  
- The number of orders and the total sales amount by Order Date  
- The number of customers who placed an order  
- The average quantity per order  
  
You need to minimize data refresh times and report query times.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Set the data type for SalesOrderNumber to Decimal Number.
Remove the CustomerKey and ProductKey columns.
Remove the TaxAmt and Freight columns.
Filter the data to only the NorthWest region sales territory.

questions.explanation:
Removing unused columns reduces the amount of data that Power BI must load and process; TaxAmt and Freight are not required for any specified analysis. Filtering the data to the NorthWest sales territory removes rows outside the report scope, reducing refresh and query workload. CustomerKey must be retained to count customers who placed orders.

**Learn more:** [Data reduction techniques for Import modeling - Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/import-modeling-data-reduction)

questions.question:
You use Power BI Desktop to open a PBIX file that contains a Microsoft Excel data source.  
  
You try to refresh the data and receive this error message:  
  
`Expression.Error: The column ‘Cost’ of the table wasn't found.`  
  
What could be causing the error?

options.text: Run the Table.buffer function in Query1.
Duplicate Query1 to all the other queries.
Reconfigure Query1 as a dataflow entity.
From the Power BI Admin portal, increase the Capacity settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft's own guidance on referenced queries states that when several queries reference a shared query like Query1, each referencing query re-executes Query1's steps independently, and explicitly warns that wrapping Query1 in Table.Buffer does not eliminate this duplicate retrieval and can even worsen performance since each referencing query buffers it separately. The recommended fix is to redesign Query1 as a dataflow entity so its data is persisted and evaluated once, which the other queries then reuse — improving refresh time without the added cost of increasing capacity.

**Learn more:** [Referencing Power Query queries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/power-query-referenced-queries)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Power BI data model that imports data from a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Power BI Desktop to load data from a Microsoft SQL Server database.

options.text: Reduce the number of rows and columns returned by each query.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing a Power BI report that uses data from an Azure SQL database named `erp1`.  
  
You import the following tables.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730275212-4fcvg83r.jpg)  
  
You need to perform these analyses:  
  
- Orders sold over time that include a measure of total order value  
- Orders by attributes of the products sold  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783730277310-9pbw6stx.png)  
  
The solution must minimize visual-interaction update times in the report.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Power Query, merge the Order Line Items query and the Products query.
Create a calculated column that adds a list of product categories to the Orders table by using a DAX function.
Calculate the count of orders per product by using a DAX function.
From Power Query, merge the Orders query and the Order Line Items query.

questions.explanation:
A fact table should store data at a consistent transaction grain and contain values that can be aggregated, while dimension tables provide attributes for filtering and grouping. Merging Orders into Order Line Items adds the order-level time attributes to the line-level quantity and price data, creating a sales fact table suitable for total-order-value measures and time analysis. Keeping Products separate allows product attributes to filter that fact table through an efficient one-to-many relationship, consistent with a star schema.

**Learn more:** [Understand star schema and the importance for Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/guidance/star-schema)

You have a Power BI report named Report1 that includes a single imported table named Sales. Sales has a column named SalesAmount and a column named OrderDate. The Sales table has 1.5 billion rows.  
  
You determine that Model1 is too large and cannot refresh within the defined time.

questions.question: Which DAX expression should be used to obtain the ending balances in balance sheet reports?

options.text: CALCULATE ( SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), LASTDATE ( 'Date'[Date] ) )
CALCULATE ( SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), DATESQTD('Date'[Date]) )
FIRSTNONBLANK ('Date'[Date] SUM( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ) )
CALCULATE ( MAX( BalanceSheet[BalanceAmount] ), LASTDATE ('Date'[Date] ))

For the relationship between Purchase Detail and Purchase, select Apply security filter in both directions.
Create one role for each country.
For the relationship between Purchase and Purchase Detail, change the Cross filter direction to Single.

questions.explanation:
A single dynamic RLS role that filters `Country[Manager_Email]` with `USERNAME()` restricts each manager to the Country row associated with their sign-in identity, minimizing role count. RLS filters use single-directional filtering by default; selecting **Apply security filter in both directions** on the Purchase Detail–Purchase relationship enables the security filter to propagate as required. In the Power BI service, `USERNAME()` returns the user's UPN, which is email-like and can match the manager email column.

**Learn more:** [Row-level security (RLS) with Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/service-admin-row-level-security)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a dataset that is rarely used and refreshes every hour.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],In Power Query Editor, you try to run a query and receive the following error:

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You publish a dataset to the Power BI service that contains a connection to an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server database.

questions.explanation: Implicit type conversion does not address case sensitivity or data integrity problems. These issues require explicit data transformation using functions like UPPER() or LOWER(), or correction at the data source level before import.

questions.question:
Solution: You add an index key and normalize casing in the data source.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.explanation:
Power BI's engine is case-insensitive, so when a DirectQuery source is case-sensitive, values differing only by letter case are treated by the source as distinct rows but by Power BI as duplicates, producing undefined values and errors. Normalizing the casing at the data source removes this mismatch, and adding an index key gives each row a stable unique identifier, together resolving the reported issue.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use composite models in Power BI Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-composite-models)

questions.explanation: Normalizing text casing using functions like UPPER() or LOWER() in Power Query standardizes data and resolves case-sensitivity discrepancies. This approach is documented in Microsoft's guidance and prevents undefined values or comparison errors in the model.

You need to ensure that screen reader users can read the value when initially interacting with the card. The value must stay updated as the dataset is refreshed.

options.text: Convert the card into a text box.

options.text: Publish an app.
Assign Group1 the Viewer role for WS1.
Store PBIX files in a shared folder in Microsoft OneDrive.
Share each item individually.

questions.explanation:
A Power BI app can grant Group1 access to a selected audience containing RPT1, RPT2, and DB1 while omitting RPT3. App audience settings can withhold permission to share the underlying semantic model and to build content from it, giving Group1 a read-only consumption experience without workspace membership. A workspace Viewer role would expose all workspace items and implicitly grants Build permission on semantic models.

**Learn more:** [Publish an app in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-create-distribute-apps) · [Semantic model permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/service-datasets-permissions)

questions.explanation: Report settings' **Personalize visuals** feature allows each user to customize their individual report view—including changing visual types—without affecting other users' experiences. Each user's personalization is saved privately to their session.

Solution: Remove the **Salesperson** table.

A fact table contains dimension key columns that establish its dimensionality. />","className":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Power BI semantic model that connects to a streaming data source. The data source is updated frequently.  
  
You need to create a Power BI report that meets the following requirements:  
  
• Supports real-time analytics  

• Minimizes performance impact on the data source  

• Displays the most recent data without performing a data refresh  
  
Which connectivity mode should you use for the dataset?

options.text: DirectQuery mode
import mode
LiveConnect mode
push mode

questions.explanation:
Push datasets receive data pushed directly into Power BI by the source application via the REST API, so the report always shows the latest values instantly with no scheduled refresh and no repeated querying of the source, minimizing load on it. DirectQuery, by contrast, must query the source every time a visual is rendered, which would increase load on a frequently updating streaming source rather than minimize it.

You need to ensure that Group1 members receive notifications when issues occur in Workspace1. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you do?

Update the contact list to include Group1.
Assign Group1 the Contributor role for Workspace1.

What should you do?

questions.question:
You are building a Power BI report that will include multiple visuals.  
  
You need to ensure the report is accessible for users who rely on a screen reader.  
  
Which two configurations should you perform? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: consistent fonts for each visual
alt text for each visual
the tab order for each page
consistent colors for each visual
Play Axis for each page

questions.explanation:
Alt text supplies a descriptive alternative for each meaningful visual that a screen reader announces when the visual receives focus. Configuring tab order on each report page provides a logical navigation sequence for keyboard and screen-reader users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Design Power BI Reports for Accessibility](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-accessibility-creating-reports)

questions.question:
You are building a Power BI report that will include multiple visuals.  
  
You need to ensure the report is accessible for users who rely on a screen reader.  
  
Which two configurations should you perform? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: A new transaction was added to the data source.
The dashboard tile cache refreshed.
A user added a comment to a tile.
A user pressed F5.

questions.explanation:
A dashboard refresh timestamp indicates that Power BI refreshed the cached data used by its tiles. Dashboard tile refresh is part of Power BI refresh processing; it does not by itself prove a new source transaction or a user action such as adding a comment or pressing F5. For Import semantic models, tiles update automatically during scheduled or on-demand data refresh.

**Learn more:** [Data refresh in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/connect-data/refresh-data)

questions.question:
Solution: You assign every user the Viewer role for the workspace.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.explanation:
The Viewer role grants read-only access to all content in a workspace, rather than to selected dashboards and reports only. This would also grant access to the remaining dashboard and reports.\
\
**Learn more:** [Roles in workspaces in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-roles-new-workspaces) · [Permission model in Microsoft Fabric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/security/permission-model)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an Azure Active Directory group that includes all users. Share each selected report and the one dashboard with the group.  
  
Does this meet the goal?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.explanation:
Power BI supports direct sharing of reports and dashboards with security groups, and shared content grants recipients read access. A security group containing all organizational users can therefore be used to grant those users access to the selected three reports and one dashboard.\
\
**Learn more:** [Share and collaborate on Power BI reports and dashboards](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-share-dashboards)

questions.question:
Solution: You publish an app to the entire organization.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.explanation:
A Power BI app packages selected dashboards and reports for a consumer audience. An app audience can be set to the entire organization, granting organizational users access to the included content. [Microsoft Learn: Publish an app in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-create-distribute-apps)\
\
**Learn more:** [Publish an app in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-create-distribute-apps)

questions.question:
Solution: Enable **Included in app** for every asset.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?

options.text: Yes
No

questions.explanation:
A Power BI app can be published to an entire organization, and its content is selected from the workspace. Including every asset would expose both dashboards and all five reports, not only the one dashboard and three reports that organizational users must be able to read. The app content must be limited to the intended assets.\
\
**Learn more:** [Publish an app in Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-create-distribute-apps)

questions.question:
You have a Power BI report with five pages.  
  
Pages 1 through 4 are visible, while page 5 is hidden.  
  
You need to create a solution that lets users quickly navigate from the first page to every other visible page. The solution must minimize development and maintenance effort as pages are added to the report.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Add a blank button to page 1.
Add a page navigation button to page 1.
Create a bookmark for each page.
Add a bookmark navigation button to page 1.

questions.explanation:
A Power BI page navigator automatically creates navigation buttons for report pages and stays synchronized when pages are added, removed, or renamed. Its page settings can exclude hidden pages, making it the lowest-maintenance option for navigation only to visible pages.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create page and bookmark navigators](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/button-navigators)

questions.question:
You are building a dashboard by using the Power BI service.  
  
You have an existing report page that includes three charts.  
  
You need to add the charts to the dashboard while preserving the interactivity between them.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Edit interactions in the report and set all interactions to Filter.
Pin each chart as a tile.
Edit the dashboard theme and pin each chart as a tile.
Pin the report page as a live tile.

questions.explanation:
A live tile created by pinning the entire report page retains the report page’s interactive behavior, including cross-filtering and cross-highlighting among its visuals. Individually pinned chart tiles are separate dashboard snapshots and do not maintain those interactions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Pin an entire report page to a Power BI dashboard as a live tile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/create-reports/service-dashboard-pin-live-tile-from-report)

questions.question:
You have a Power BI semantic model that contains two queries.  
  
You discover that a report based on the model has performance issues.  
  
You plan to use Power Query to reduce the data loaded to the model.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct answer is worth one point.

options.text: Apply group by and summarize techniques.
Combine the queries by using Append.
Remove unnecessary columns and rows.
Combine the queries by using Merge.
Create a new query group.

questions.explanation: Applying group by and summarize techniques (A) reduces data by aggregating it, and removing unnecessary columns and rows (C) directly decreases the dataset size. Both actions reduce the volume of data loaded to the model, improving performance. Appending and merging queries combine data without reducing size. Query groups are organizational tools only and do not affect performance.

questions.question:

In Report1, you change the **Sales by month** visual to a bar chart.  
  
You need to make sure that the bar chart appears on Dashboard1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Formatting tab, select Values, and then set URL icons to On for the table.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a Power BI workspace containing a supplier quality dashboard. The dashboard includes 10 card visuals, two map visuals, and five bar chart visuals.

You need to change the dashboard mobile layout to meet these requirements:  
  
- Show only single-value visuals.  
- Minimize scrolling.  
  
What should you do?
